title: Managing water scarcity in Australia
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:17Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches Australia's responses to water scarcity; the closest card, Managing water sustainably, covers only general methods like grey water, stormwater and desalination, so the new point would need content it lacks (dams, restrictions, efficient irrigation, Murray-Darling trading).

draft.title: Managing water scarcity in Australia
card: Australia is a dry continent, so it uses many ways to make sure people have enough water. Some add to supply and some reduce demand.
Dams store rainfall. Desalination plants remove salt from seawater. Recycled water is treated used water. Rainwater tanks collect rain from roofs.
Water restrictions limit how much water people can use, such as watering gardens. Efficient irrigation, such as drip systems, gives crops only the water they need.
In the Murray-Darling Basin, water entitlements can be bought and sold between users. Water can then move to the users who value it most.
draft.remember: Australia manages scarcity by adding supply, cutting demand and trading water between users.

a.q: Which of these is a way of cutting demand for water?
opts: Limiting garden watering in a dry spell
Building a dam to store rainfall
Treating used water so it can be reused
a.why: Water restrictions reduce how much water people use, so they cut demand. Dams, recycling and desalination all add to the supply of water instead.
a.clue: Which one asks people to use less?

b.q: A drought hits a farming town in the Murray-Darling Basin. Tom's orchard needs more water. Jess has water she does not need this season. Which method lets Tom get water from Jess?
b.why: Water trading lets users in the Basin buy and sell water entitlements, so Tom can buy from Jess. Restrictions are tempting, but they limit use and do not move water between users.
b.clue: One method involves buying and selling.

a.best: Limiting garden watering in a dry spell
